description: Shared module shared/lib/tickets/boardFieldRules.ts with plain functions taking a knex connection or transaction and a tenant; exported through shared/package.json and shared/tsup.config.ts
Impact x Urgency matrix moves to shared/lib/itil/priorityMatrix.ts; packages/tickets itilUtils re-exports calculateItilPriority and ItilLabels from it
listPrioritiesForBoard returns ticket priorities whose family matches the board's priority_type, ordered, including itil_priority_level

findBoardFieldProblems checks a priority against a board's priority_type and returns a field-level problem naming the priority and the board; the PR #3880 helpers in ticketFieldReferences delegate to it
findTicketPatchBoardFieldProblems checks the priority only when the patch changes priority_id or board_id, and the category only when it changes category_id, subcategory_id or board_id
resolveItilPriorityId returns the tenant's ITIL priority for an Impact x Urgency pair by itil_priority_level, never by name
defaultPriorityForBoard returns the board default when it fits, else the level-3 ITIL priority or the lowest-order own ticket priority, else null
resolveTicketPriorityFields applies R4 for a create or an update and returns priority_id, itil_impact and itil_urgency; takes a policy of refuse or fallback
With policy fallback, resolveTicketPriorityFields returns the configured priority when it fits, else the board default, else the configured priority unchanged
On a board with the tenant's own priorities, resolveTicketPriorityFields returns empty Impact and Urgency whatever was supplied
ITIL priority seeding finds existing rows by family and level; it never flags an existing unflagged priority by name, and a name collision with a tenant priority is reported with the priority's name
Inbound ticket defaults form lists only priorities that fit the selected board
Changing the board in the inbound ticket defaults form clears a selected priority that no longer fits
Saving inbound ticket defaults refuses a priority of the wrong family or one that no longer exists, with a field error
A stored inbound default whose priority does not fit its board or no longer exists shows a warning in the form and a badge in the defaults list
Inbound email ticket creation resolves its priority with policy fallback
New inbound-defaults strings use translation keys in every locale; new controls have kebab-case ids
Integration fixture that builds a tenant with one non-ITIL board, two ITIL boards, one legacy mixed board, both priority families and own categories
Table-driven suite itilSecondBoardSurfaces listing every picker and writer from the PRD; each surface is marked expected-fail until its commit group lands
Migration adds categories.standard_category_id (nullable uuid)
Migration links each flagged category to its standard row by name and parent name
Migration clears is_from_itil_standard on rows that cannot be linked or sit on a board whose categories are not ITIL
Migration inserts the missing standard rows for every ITIL board that has no set of its own, parents before children
Migration re-points tickets.category_id and subcategory_id on other ITIL boards to that board's copy of the same standard category
Migration re-points ticket_templates, recurring definitions (columns, overrides and client overrides) and inbound_ticket_defaults the same way

Migration re-points category ids in JSON settings that name both a board and a category (workflow action inputs, Huntress settings, inbound webhook mappings, checklist rules); settings without a board are left
Migration adds a partial unique index on (tenant, board_id, standard_category_id) where the link is set
Migration is idempotent, runs per tenant, uses the self-contained tenantDb shim, selects values before updating by parameter, and sets transaction false
Migration changes no ticket's priority, Impact or Urgency and no category on the board that holds the set today
Dev seeds create the ITIL board before the ITIL categories and seed the set onto that board
listCategoriesForBoard returns the categories whose board_id is the board, for ITIL and non-ITIL boards alike, with standard_category_id
getTicketCategoriesByBoard, the ticket-form hydration in optimizedTicketActions and GET /api/v1/tickets/categories call listCategoriesForBoard; the list-by-flag branch is removed
findBoardFieldProblems checks that a category's board is the ticket's board and that a subcategory is a child of the category
The separate category checks in ticketFieldReferences, co-managed ticketEditing and the asset maintenance workflow action are replaced by the shared check
ItilStandardsService gives a board its standard set by inserting the standard rows that board lacks, keyed by standard_category_id; it never reads or changes another board's categories
Board delete removes the board's categories with it; the re-pointing step and the category half of cleanupUnusedItilStandards are removed
A standard row on an ITIL board cannot be renamed, re-parented, moved or deleted through web actions
A standard row on an ITIL board cannot be changed or deleted through REST CategoryService or the reference-data delete
Adding a category to an ITIL board is refused in web settings and REST create
copyTicketCategoriesToBoard accepts only a non-ITIL target board and copies rows without the standard link or flag
updateTicketCategory accepts only name, display order and parent
deleteCategory, updateCategory, updateTicketCategory and deleteReferenceDataItem for categories require the ticket_settings permission
REST deleteTicketCategory refuses a category in use as a subcategory
Categories settings shows an ITIL board's own set with a Standard badge, disables edit, delete and add there, and offers only non-ITIL boards as copy targets
CSV import matches categories within the row's board and, on an ITIL board, reports an unmatched category per row instead of creating it

Pickers that filter categories by board list the standard set on every ITIL board: co-managed edit, inbound email defaults, workflow designer (both copies), Huntress settings, inbound webhook mapping, checklist rules, REST category list, tree and search, onboarding
New category strings use translation keys in every locale; new controls have kebab-case ids
MSP ticket create computes the ITIL priority only when the board has ITIL priorities, through resolveTicketPriorityFields
Both MSP ticket update functions use resolveTicketPriorityFields; the four name-pattern lookups are removed
A direct priority change on an ITIL ticket that has Impact and Urgency sets them to the diagonal pair for the new level
A write that supplies only one of Impact and Urgency is refused on interactive paths
Service request provider, template instantiation, the recurring generator and batch duplicate resolve priority and Impact/Urgency through the shared function
itil_priority_level is no longer accepted in the ticket schema or written; event payloads and list queries take the level from the priority row
Ticket detail, the bento hero and quick add show the stored priority and Not assessed when an ITIL ticket has no Impact and Urgency
New Impact/Urgency strings use translation keys in every locale
TicketModel.createTicket takes a field policy and runs the priority and category rules inside the model, so every create that reaches it is covered
Client portal ticket create refuses a priority that does not fit the board
CSV import checks priority and category per row against the row's board and reports failures per row; its fallback priority is the board default
Teams message action, Teams guest intake and manual telephony tickets take their priority from defaultPriorityForBoard
Workflow assets.create_maintenance_ticket refuses a priority or category that does not fit the board
RMM alert ticket creation resolves its priority with policy fallback and filters priorities by item type
Huntress incident ticket creation resolves its priority with policy fallback and drops a category that is not the board's
Telephony auto-ticket and contract renewal ticket resolve their priority with policy fallback
Workflow tickets.create and inbound webhook create resolve priority with policy fallback and drop a category that is not the board's
Service request provider falls back to the board default priority, filtered to ticket priorities
Data-migration import resolves priority with policy fallback
REST v1 create and create-from-asset check the category against the board
prepareTicketFieldPatch in the shared module validates and normalises the priority, Impact, Urgency, category and subcategory of an update patch against the current ticket
MSP updateTicket and updateTicketInTransaction call prepareTicketFieldPatch before writing
REST v1 ticket update calls prepareTicketFieldPatch, including the subcategory-to-category check it lacks today
TicketModel.updateTicket calls prepareTicketFieldPatch, covering workflow tickets.update_fields and inbound webhook update
Both Activities inline priority updates check the priority against the ticket's board
Bundle sync does not copy the master's priority onto a child whose board has the other priority family
A board move requires a priority that fits the destination when the families differ, and clears Impact and Urgency when the destination has the tenant's own priorities
A board move between two ITIL boards maps the category and subcategory to the destination's copy of the same standard category; any other board move without a category in the patch clears them
A ticket whose stored priority or category does not fit its board saves changes to title, status, assignee and description
One client helper filters a priority list for a board; QuickAddTicket, TicketInfo, BentoHero, BoardsSettings, surveys TriggerForm and TicketImportDialog use it instead of their own copies
Workflow designer priority options carry their family and are filtered by the selected board, in both copies of the picker
Huntress settings list priorities that fit the selected board
Co-managed ticket edit lists and accepts only priorities that fit the ticket's board
Service request editor lists priorities that fit the selected board, for both board kinds
Create ticket from asset lists priorities that fit the selected board
Activities inline priority picker lists priorities that fit the ticket's board
CSV import dialog maps priorities using each row's board, not the default board
Inbound webhook mapping and RMM alert rule lookups return ticket priorities only; the webhook lookup filters by the mapped board
GET /api/v1/tickets/priorities accepts board_id and returns itil_priority_level
Mobile ticket detail lists priorities by the board's kind instead of the current priority's family
Board create, update and delete logic is extracted from the server actions into plain functions taking a transaction, tenant and actor; the actions add only authentication
REST BoardService create, update and delete call those functions
Board create inserts the board, runs ITIL setup, then picks the default priority, then seeds statuses
A supplied default_priority_id is checked against the board's priority family on create and update
Creating a board with different category and priority kinds is refused on web and REST
An update that changes either kind to a mixed combination is refused; an existing mixed board still saves other edits
default_assigned_team_id is saved on board create
Board create returns, and BOARD_CREATED carries, the row as it is after setup
Reference-data board import and the onboarding board insert go through the shared create function
REST board delete refuses with the same reasons as the web delete
switchBoardType sets both kinds of a board to ITIL or to the tenant's own, behind the ticket_settings permission
Switching to ITIL ensures the tenant's ITIL priorities, gives the board its standard categories and resets its default priority to a fitting one; categories already on the board stay
Switching to the tenant's own kind keeps the board's categories as ordinary editable categories and resets its default priority to a fitting one
A switch changes no ticket, inbound default, template, schedule or SLA assignment
A pre-switch summary counts the open tickets, inbound defaults, templates and schedules on the board whose priority will not fit
Switching to the tenant's own kind is refused with a message when the tenant has no ticket priorities of its own
Boards settings edit dialog has a Change board type action with a confirmation showing the summary; a legacy mixed board shows both kinds read-only
Board update no longer changes kinds on its own; a REST PUT with a changed kind runs the switch
New board-type strings use translation keys in every locale; new controls have kebab-case ids
registerSlaIntegration runs from initializeApp and is asserted registered at startup; the call in WorkspaceRouteLayout is removed
ITIL setup on a PSA tenant fails with an error when the SLA hook is not registered, instead of skipping
Migration adds sla_policies.is_itil_standard, sets it on the existing policy named ITIL Standard, and allows at most one per tenant
itilSlaService, the cleanup in ItilStandardsService and ensureSlaParity find the ITIL policy by the flag, not the name
Creating an ITIL board when the ITIL policy already exists adds targets for ITIL priorities that have none and leaves existing targets unchanged
One module in shared holds the ITIL SLA default targets and thresholds; itilSlaService and product-upgrade-operations import it
Only board creation assigns the ITIL policy; board update, the type switch and migrations never assign a policy
TICKET_SLA_STAGE events are built from the ticket's SLA start and resolution due time; a ticket without an SLA emits none; shared/lib/itil/slaTargets.ts is deleted
server/src/lib/utils/itilUtils.ts and packages/tickets/src/lib/itilUtils.server.ts are deleted
Unused exports are removed from packages/tickets itilUtils
getAvailablePriorities, getAvailableCategories and the stray console.log are removed from ticketFieldOptionsActions
The unused category lister in server/src/lib/models/ticketCategory.tsx and the unused raw ticket insert in shared/services/emailService.ts are removed after confirming no callers
display_itil_impact and display_itil_urgency are removed from board schemas, types and writes, and dropped by migration

scripts/guard-ticket-board-field-rules.mjs fails on a direct read of priorities or categories, or a direct write of a ticket's priority, category or board, outside an allow-list; wired as an npm script and a CI step
Contract test asserts every writer module listed in the PRD imports the shared rules
docs/itil/itil-integration.md is rewritten to describe the rules, the data model and the board lifecycle as built
docs/itil/ITIL_Integration_Plan.md moves to docs/archive
scripts/reports/priority-board-mismatch.sql category sections compare the category's board with the ticket's board
OpenAPI is regenerated for the board, category, priority and ticket schema changes
